---
title: "QoS Profiles for PX4 Topics"
---

ROS 2 Quality of Service (QoS) settings must match between publisher and
subscriber. PX4 publishes all `/fmu/out/*` topics with **BEST_EFFORT**
reliability. If your subscriber uses the default **RELIABLE** profile, ROS 2
silently drops the connection — the subscription is created with no error, but
the callback never fires.

---

## Why QoS mismatches are silent

ROS 2 DDS does not error on a QoS incompatibility. The subscription is
registered, the topic appears in `ros2 topic list`, but the middleware
determines the publisher and subscriber are incompatible and simply sends no
data. `ros2 topic hz` reports 0 Hz.

---

## PX4 publisher profile

All PX4 `/fmu/out/*` topics use:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Reliability | `BEST_EFFORT` |
| Durability | `VOLATILE` |
| History | `KEEP_LAST(10)` |

**BEST_EFFORT** means packets may be dropped under load — acceptable for
high-rate sensor streams where stale data is worse than missing data.
**VOLATILE** means the publisher does not persist messages for late-joining
subscribers.

---

## Subscriber QoS

Match the publisher profile exactly:

```cpp
#include <rclcpp/qos.hpp>

// Correct: matches PX4 publisher profile
auto qos = rclcpp::QoS(10).best_effort();

sub_ = create_subscription<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleOdometry>(
    "/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry", qos, callback);
```

The `rclcpp::QoS(10)` constructor sets history depth to 10 and defaults
durability to `VOLATILE`. `.best_effort()` switches reliability from the
default `RELIABLE` to `BEST_EFFORT`.

::: {.callout-warning}
The ROS 2 default QoS (`rclcpp::SystemDefaultsQoS()` or
`rclcpp::QoS(rclcpp::KeepLast(10))`) uses `RELIABLE` reliability.
Using it for PX4 subscriptions results in silent starvation.
:::

---

## Publisher QoS (ROS 2 -> PX4)

For `/fmu/in/*` topics (commands sent **to** PX4), use the same profile:

```cpp
auto qos = rclcpp::QoS(10).best_effort();

pub_ = create_publisher<px4_msgs::msg::OffboardControlMode>(
    "/fmu/in/offboard_control_mode", qos);
```

PX4's DDS client subscribes to these topics with BEST_EFFORT. A RELIABLE
publisher will time out waiting for acknowledgements that never come.

---

## Convenience wrapper

Define a single helper to avoid repeating the QoS setup:

```cpp
/* px4_qos.hpp */
#pragma once
#include <rclcpp/qos.hpp>

inline rclcpp::QoS px4_qos(std::size_t depth = 10) {
    return rclcpp::QoS(depth).best_effort();
}
```

Usage:

```cpp
#include "my_package/px4_qos.hpp"

odom_sub_   = create_subscription<...>("/fmu/out/...", px4_qos(), cb);
cmd_pub_    = create_publisher<...>   ("/fmu/in/...",  px4_qos());
```

---

## Diagnosing a mismatch

```bash
# Check publisher QoS
ros2 topic info /fmu/out/vehicle_odometry --verbose

# Expected:
# Publisher count: 1
#   QoS profile:
#     Reliability: BEST_EFFORT
#     Durability: VOLATILE
```

If your subscriber shows `Reliability: RELIABLE` while the publisher shows
`BEST_EFFORT`, the middleware will log an incompatibility warning at the `DEBUG`
level. Enable it:

```bash
export RCUTILS_LOGGING_SEVERITY=DEBUG
ros2 run my_package my_node
# look for: "NEW_QOS_POLICY_REQUEST_INCOMPATIBLE_QOS"
```

---

## Python subscribers

The same rule applies to `rclpy`:

```python
from rclpy.qos import QoSProfile, ReliabilityPolicy, DurabilityPolicy

px4_qos = QoSProfile(
    reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.BEST_EFFORT,
    durability=DurabilityPolicy.VOLATILE,
    depth=10,
)

self.sub = self.create_subscription(
    VehicleOdometry,
    "/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry",
    self.callback,
    px4_qos,
)
```

---

## Summary

| Topic direction | Reliability | Durability |
|-----------------|-------------|------------|
| `/fmu/out/*` (PX4 -> ROS 2) | BEST_EFFORT | VOLATILE |
| `/fmu/in/*`  (ROS 2 -> PX4) | BEST_EFFORT | VOLATILE |

Use `.best_effort()` on every QoS object that touches a PX4 topic. There are
no exceptions.
